parsed.why: Fresh 2025 criminalisation under military rule: 2–5 years' imprisonment, deportation of foreigners stated, plus 'promotion' ban, no anti-discrimination ground, no recourse, hostile religious/traditional climate. No enforcement record yet, but the statute is explicit and state-directed: high risk.

Decriminalised by courts (2018), no trans criminalisation, but no legal gender recognition, no hate-crime law, documented dating-app ambush robberies and 'beaten, stoned' community reports with thin recourse, and unsafe prison placement. Elevated risk: societal hostility with weak remedies.

Strong formal framework (notary LGR, court protections, decrees) but documented pattern of lethal trans violence — armed-group kill lists, 40+ trans women killed in 2023, killings rising with accountability gaps; general homicide is high so partly background. Working recourse mitigates; elevated risk.

No criminalisation and some protective asylum machinery naming trans people, but recent (2025) documented police harassment at identity checks and arbitrary arrests of trans people, NGOs barred from registering, no anti-discrimination ground. Elevated risk: state-adjacent targeting at the encounters travellers actually face.

Strong operating protections: 2024 hate-crime statute, Equality Court ordering gender-affirming detention care (Nov 2025), LGR since 2003, favourable attitudes. Offset by township hate violence, uneven facility protection and police friction. Reduced risk — best of the five but not low.
